metadata.course_description: A comprehensive study of fundamental data structures, abstract data types, algorithm analysis, sorting, searching, and advanced tree and graph algorithms designed for scalable software development.

course_outcomes.statement: Analyze the asymptotic time and space complexity of fundamental algorithms and data structures.
Implement dynamic linear and non-linear data structures in high-level programming languages.
Design robust and memory-efficient software components to resolve complex computational problems.
Demonstrate professional collaboration and adherence to coding ethical standards in team projects.

topics: Institutional Orientation and Pointers/Memory Management Review

intended_learning_outcomes.statement: Explain course outcomes, grading standards, and memory pointer semantics.
Configure the compiler toolchain and implement basic pointer manipulation programs.
Internalize safety protocols and collaborative etiquette in computer laboratories.

topics: Algorithm Analysis and Asymptotic Notation (Big-O, Big-Omega, Big-Theta)

intended_learning_outcomes.statement: Differentiate between worst, average, and best-case algorithmic efficiencies.
Calculate asymptotic complexity equations for iterative code fragments.
Appraise the practical significance of algorithmic performance optimization.

topics: Linear Abstract Data Types: Dynamic Arrays and Vector Internals

intended_learning_outcomes.statement: Describe dynamic array resizing and amortized cost mechanics.
Construct a custom generic dynamic array with dynamic memory management.
Demonstrate diligence in checking array bounds and preventing memory leaks.

resources_references: Data Structures and Algorithm Analysis in C++ (Mark Weiss)

topics: Linked Lists: Singly and Doubly Linked Architectures

intended_learning_outcomes.statement: Compare linked list node allocation with contiguous array indexing.
Implement pointer linking, node insertion, and deletion algorithms.
Value disciplined code commenting when writing complex pointer references.

assessment_tasks: Machine Problem 3: Doubly Linked List ADT
resources_references: Data Structures and Algorithms in Python (Goodrich et al.)

topics: Circular Linked Lists and Skip List Fundamentals

intended_learning_outcomes.statement: Explain the operational mechanics of circular lists in round-robin scheduling.
Execute circular traversal algorithms without triggering infinite loops.
Exhibit methodical debugging strategies when troubleshooting pointer cycles.

topics: Stack ADT: LIFO Principles and Expression Evaluation

intended_learning_outcomes.statement: Identify stack mechanics in nested function calls and expression parsing.
Implement infix-to-postfix expression conversion and postfix evaluation.
Display attention to boundary condition checks such as stack overflow.

topics: Queue ADT: FIFO, Circular Buffers, and Deques

intended_learning_outcomes.statement: Explain the advantages of circular queue arrays over naive linear queues.
Develop thread-safe circular buffer primitives for producer-consumer pipelines.
Recognize the importance of buffer management in high-throughput services.

assessment_tasks: Machine Problem 5: Print Spooler Queue Simulation

intended_learning_outcomes.statement: Formulate recurrence relations using the Master Theorem.
Construct recursive and backtracking algorithms (e.g., N-Queens, Towers of Hanoi).
Demonstrate patience and methodical tracing of recursion call trees.

topics: Midterm Assessment and Laboratory Practical Examination

intended_learning_outcomes.statement: Integrate theoretical knowledge of linear data structures and asymptotic limits.
Solve complex pointer-based data structure challenges within a timed environment.
Adhere strictly to academic honesty and institutional testing protocols.

resources_references: Course Lecture Notes and Laboratory Exercises

topics: Hierarchical Data Structures: General Trees and Binary Trees

intended_learning_outcomes.statement: Categorize tree topologies, node degrees, heights, and levels.
Implement recursive preorder, inorder, postorder, and level-order tree traversals.
Value recursive elegance in managing non-linear topologies.

topics: Binary Search Trees (BST): Search, Insertion, and Deletion

intended_learning_outcomes.statement: Explain the BST invariant and performance degradation under unbalanced inputs.
Execute node deletion algorithms handling leaf, single-child, and two-child cases.
Commit to rigorous edge-case testing during algorithm verification.

topics: Self-Balancing Trees: AVL Trees and Tree Rotations

intended_learning_outcomes.statement: Calculate balance factors and determine Single (LL, RR) and Double (LR, RL) rotations.
Implement self-balancing insertion routines maintaining O(log n) guarantees.
Demonstrate perseverance when tackling intricate rotational pointer operations.

assessment_tasks: Machine Problem 8: AVL Tree Self-Balancing Engine

topics: Priority Queues and Binary Heaps (Min-Heap / Max-Heap)

intended_learning_outcomes.statement: Explain array-based binary heap indexing and heapify procedures.
Implement heap-extract-max and bubble-up operations for priority scheduling.
Prioritize cache-friendly array representation in systems engineering.

assessment_tasks: Machine Problem 9: Hospital Triage Priority System

topics: Graph Theory: Representations via Adjacency Matrix and Adjacency Lists

intended_learning_outcomes.statement: Analyze time-space trade-offs between sparse and dense graph storage representations.
Construct generic weighted directed and undirected graph classes.
Demonstrate collaboration in designing shared graph data structures.

topics: Graph Traversal Algorithms: Breadth-First Search (BFS) and Depth-First Search (DFS)

intended_learning_outcomes.statement: Differentiate shortest path BFS applications from backtracking DFS implementations.
Implement topological sorting and cycle detection algorithms on directed graphs.
Cultivate methodical analysis when evaluating interconnected real-world networks.

topics: Hashing Techniques, Hash Functions, and Collision Resolution

intended_learning_outcomes.statement: Evaluate collision mitigation strategies: Separate Chaining vs. Open Addressing.
Implement custom hash map tables with dynamic load factor rehashing.
Defend the critical role of secure hash distribution against algorithmic attacks.

topics: Advanced Sorting (Quicksort, Mergesort) and System Integration

intended_learning_outcomes.statement: Contrast comparison-based lower bounds O(n log n) with linear non-comparison sorts.
Optimize 3-way partitioning Quicksort and combine multi-threaded sorting routines.
Demonstrate professional accountability and teamwork in project integration.

topics: Final Institutional Examination and Capstone Project Defense

intended_learning_outcomes.statement: Synthesize data structure tradeoffs across large-scale software architectures.
Defend architectural decisions, algorithmic complexity, and test results live.
Display ethical composure and professional communication during oral examination.

resources_references: Course Project Guidelines and Repository Archive
